name: Crying Tiger (Thai-Style Grilled Steak With Dry Chili Dipping Sauce)

ingredients.name: eye York strip steaks, about 1 1/2-inches thick

instructions.primary_message: Mix together the soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, and vegetable oil in a medium mixing bowl. Coat the steaks with the soy sauce mixture and let them marinate while you work on the dipping sauce.
Combine all ingredients for the dipping sauce in a small bowl and mix. If using, peel and deseed the tomatoes. Chop the pulp finely, and add it to prepared dried chile dipping sauce; set aside.

Light one chimney full of charcoal. When all the charcoal is lit and covered with gray ash, pour out and spread the coals evenly over entire surface of coal grate. Set cooking grate in place, cover grill and allow to preheat for 5 minutes. Alternatively, set all the burners on a gas grill to high heat. Clean and oil the grilling grate.

Grill the steaks, turning frequently, until desired doneness is reached (medium-rare is recommended—steaks should register 52°C on an instant read thermometer when removed from grill). Remove from grill and let rest for 5 minutes. (See the importance of resting meat).
Cut the steaks into 0.5-cm slices and serve with the dipping sauce. Warm sticky rice on the side is highly recommended.

schema_metadata.keywords: dipping sauces, jaew, my thai, tiger cry

description: The grilled aroma of the steak and the smokiness of the piquant dipping sauce contribute to the appeal of this classic dish.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 plum tomatoes (optional)

Optional substitutions: light brown sugar → dark brown sugar; eye York strip steaks → New York strip steaks

Notes: Although any cut of beef that is well suited for grilling will work for this recipe, rib eye and New York strip are recommended.
author: Leela Punyaratabandhu
